theme: Unit 24 review, Faith Lived Out, General Epistles
memoryText: We love because he first loved us.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This short verse is the heart of the General Epistles. James told us that faith without works is dead, Peter told us to love one another earnestly, John told us that God is love, and Jude told us to keep ourselves in the love of God. Where does that love begin? Not in us. “We love because he first loved us.”

The love of God came first, in the cross: “In this is love, not that we have loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins.” Our love for God and for each other is the echo of his. We are not trying to earn love; we are responding to a love already given.

This is freeing. On days when we feel unloving, we do not manufacture love by willpower. We look again at the love that came first, and let it fill us and overflow. Say this verse slowly, and thank him for loving you first.
unitRecap: This unit took us through the General Epistles, which ask what genuine faith looks like in real life. James taught that faith is tested by trials and shown by works: we are to be doers of the word, tame the tongue by God’s grace, show no partiality, and pray with patience. Psalms 12, 15, and 24 deepened this with the purity of the LORD’s words, the character of those who dwell with God, and the King of glory who alone has clean hands and a pure heart. We paused to consider saving faith: knowing, agreeing, trusting, and how faith alone is never alone. First Peter gave us a living hope, our identity as a chosen race, royal priesthood, and holy nation, the example of Christ’s suffering, and the call to cast our anxieties on God while resisting the roaring lion. Second Peter reminded us that God has given us everything for life and godliness, that Scripture is breathed out by the Spirit, and that the Lord’s delay is patience. We paused on the canon: why we have sixty-six books. Psalms 34, 118, and 31 invited us to taste and see, to give thanks for steadfast love, and to commit our spirit to God’s hand. First John gave tests of genuine faith: walking in the light, confessing sin, loving the brothers, believing in the incarnate Son, and knowing that we have eternal life. We paused on perseverance and assurance. Second John and Third John showed truth and love in hospitality, and Jude called us to contend for the faith once delivered and trust the God who is able to keep us from stumbling.

reviewQuestions.question: How does James reconcile “faith without works is dead” with justification by faith alone?
reviewQuestions.prompt: In your own words, explain how Paul and James fit together, and give one example of faith showing itself in works.

reviewQuestions.question: What does Peter mean by “a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation”?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Write what these titles tell you about who you are as a Christian, and how they shape how you live as an exile.

reviewQuestions.question: What are the tests of genuine faith in 1 John?
reviewQuestions.prompt: List the tests John gives, and choose one you want to grow in this month.

reviewQuestions.question: What does Jude mean when he says to “contend for the faith”?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Describe what it looks like to contend for the faith with both truth and mercy, using verses 20 to 23.

prayerPrompts: Thank God for loving you first.
Thank him for what the General Epistles have taught you about living the faith.
Ask him to keep the unit verse before you.
